meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start there.
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

You don't have time for this, Hale, and you're the one who asked for this meeting. On what basis does the zero stand, and was Owen heard before you entered it? Answer that, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

Show me the line, and show me the outline. A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a citation error, and students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, so that is what I'll be checking. Turn the screen, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that I receive an apology for the mark being entered before anyone called me, and that nothing about this goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a guarantee that nothing goes on his record, and the fair outcome she never reached is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, because the meeting ended before her time ran out or the evidence was shown.
What moved her: Naming a quotation that is not in Hamlet and an October 15 outline arguing a different thesis moved her slightly, because both were specific, dated, tied to his own work, and something she could check herself, so she stopped threatening and asked to see them.
What cost ground: Opening by saying you had no time and the zero stands cost you ground, because it gave her a decision with no basis and confirmed her belief that the school punishes first and explains later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence came nowhere near a late night, since the only date you raised was the October 15 outline, and that night proves nothing about the essay, it only explains why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, take responsibility in one sentence for entering it before calling her, then put the misquoted line and the outline on the screen before she has to ask.
